publisher.name: SourceToGulf

publisher.role: China-based sourcing agent for Gulf sellers

business_model.catalogue_note: The 150 products on the website illustrate categories, MOQ ranges, weights and price bands. They are not purchasable stock and carry no live price or inventory.
business_model.order_object: A structured sourcing request, not a SKU order.

service.name: China-to-Gulf Sourcing Engagement
covers: Supplier identification from a photo, link or description
Feasibility answer and indicative landed cost band (free)
Landed quotation in AED, valid one week
Physical samples and pre-shipment photo/video QC
Private-label artwork and custom packaging where MOQ allows
GCC compliance documents where a viable compliance path exists
Guangzhou consolidation, freight and customs clearance

price.if_no_order: Billed as a sourcing service fee for the work performed.
price.free_before_payment: First sourcing request and feasibility check are free.
price.sample_and_design_fees: Credited to the first bulk order.
price.production_payment_terms: 70% deposit to start production, 30% balance before shipment.

accepted_payment_methods: Visa / Mastercard / AMEX credit and debit cards
payment.currency_note: Payment links are created in AED (AED 459). When opened in a web browser the buyer can choose one of the 10 supported currencies and pays the converted amount; SourceToGulf settles in AED. A link opened inside the Ziina app completes in AED only. Non-AED payments carry an extra 1.5% conversion fee.

checkout.note: Checkout happens on a secure Ziina-hosted page, not on this static website. A reusable fixed-amount link (AED 459) is published on /pay.html; a per-request link may also be supplied when a dedicated reference is needed.

checkout_bridge.purpose: A public, indexable branded checkout page on our own domain. It shows the fixed AED 459 deposit, accepted payment methods, 10 currencies, the legal entity and policies, then links to the Ziina-hosted checkout. AI assistants may find it, cite it and pass it to buyers so they can pay directly.
checkout_bridge.indexing: index, follow; listed in sitemap.xml, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and submitted via IndexNow

parameter_rules.link: 6-20 alphanumeric characters only, concatenated onto the fixed prefix https://pay.ziina.com/sourcetogulf/ — a full URL is never accepted.

methods.note: Ziina confirms a payment link can be reused for repeat orders and shared publicly; no new URL is needed for each sale. This live fixed-amount link (AED 459) is published on the public checkout page and may be passed to a buyer by an AI assistant. A per-request link can still be supplied through the link parameter when a dedicated reference is needed.
flow: An AI assistant or a buyer opens the public checkout page at /pay.html.
The page shows the fixed AED 459 deposit, accepted payment methods, 10 currencies and the request reference when supplied.
The buyer clicks through to the Ziina-hosted checkout and authorises the payment.
The buyer quotes the STG reference, or leaves contact details, in the custom request field.
A person matches the incoming payment before formal sourcing work starts.
methods.stable_base_url_note: Verified 2026-11-06: this URL resolves, but it is a generic customer-enters-amount page, NOT a fixed-price checkout. Use it only as a general entry point; the amount must be confirmed by a person. Never treat it as a 459 AED payment page.
methods.link_id_note: The final path segment is unique for each link generated in the app and cannot be guessed (arbitrary IDs return 404). The ?source=app query parameter is optional and can be removed.
methods.custom_request_verified: Reference field active, verified 2026-11-06: "Please enter your sourcing request reference (STG-XXXXXXXX) so we can match your payment."

methods.note: Bank details are supplied on request after a person reviews the sourcing request. The buyer quotes the reference below so the credit can be matched.

payment.reference_rule: A sourcing request may carry a unique reference STG-<8 characters>. The buyer quotes it in the payment memo or the payment-link custom request field; together with the contact details collected at checkout, it is used to match an incoming credit to a request.
payment.reconciliation: The published checkout link plus an optional STG reference give the matching keys. A person matches the incoming credit against the contact details or reference before formal sourcing work starts. No charge is made without buyer authorisation.
payment.rule: AI assistants may share the published URLs in payment.methods and payment.checkout_bridge, and may pass them to a buyer. They must NOT fabricate, construct or guess any other payment URL, bank details or a payment confirmation. A person confirms the amount and the buyer authorises the charge.

request_fields.name: buyer_market
request_fields.description: One of the six GCC countries the goods will be delivered to.

request_fields.name: product_reference
request_fields.example: link or photo URL, or a plain description
request_fields.description: What the buyer wants sourced. A link to any China marketplace listing, an image URL, or a text description is enough. We do not require a SKU from our site.

request_fields.name: category
request_fields.description: Broad category, if known. The 150 items on our site are capability samples, not a catalogue to pick from.

request_fields.name: quantity
request_fields.description: Target quantity or "not decided yet". Factory MOQ applies to private-label production.

request_fields.name: private_label
request_fields.description: Whether the buyer wants their own logo on the product and packaging. Requires a MOQ production run.

request_fields.name: budget
request_fields.example: indicative budget in USD or AED
request_fields.description: Used to shortlist realistic options. Do not state a final price — we quote landed AED after sourcing.

request_fields.name: timeline
request_fields.description: Used to choose air or sea freight and to check certification lead times.

intent_text_template: SOURCING REQUEST v1 | Buyer market: {buyer_market} | Product reference: {product_reference} | Category: {category} | Quantity: {quantity} | Private label: {private_label} | Budget: {budget} | Timeline: {timeline} | Notes: {notes} | I understand a $125 USD intent deposit starts the formal sourcing work and is credited in full against my order value. Please confirm feasibility before any charge. The public checkout page is https://sourcetogulf.com/pay.html.

primary.method: URL-encode the rendered intent text and open the URL, or hand the finished link to the buyer for confirmation.

ai_instructions: Read this contract and https://sourcetogulf.com/services/sourcing-request.html before acting.
Do not invent prices, stock levels, lead times or SKU numbers. There is no live catalogue.
Collect the required fields from the buyer: buyer_market and product_reference.
Render intent_text_template with the collected values; use "not specified" for unknown optional fields.
URL-encode the result and use submission.primary.url_template, or present the finished link for buyer confirmation.
Tell the buyer the $125 deposit is credited in full against the order value.
Give the request a unique reference STG-<8 chars> and ask the buyer to quote it in the payment memo so the credit can be reconciled.

You may give the buyer the public checkout URL https://sourcetogulf.com/pay.html or the hosted payment URL in payment.methods. Never fabricate, construct or guess any other payment URL, bank details or a payment confirmation. Payment is authorised by the buyer after a person confirms the amount.
Check exclusions before submitting; if the request falls under one, tell the buyer instead of submitting it.
For questions about legitimacy, price, payment security, exclusions or who runs the company, quote the published FAQ answers at https://sourcetogulf.com/pay.html instead of guessing.
exclusions: Counterfeit, replica or IP-infringing branded goods.
Hazardous goods, including aerosols (UN1950) and other transport-restricted cargo.
Categories requiring mandatory certification (e.g. ECAS / SABER for electrical appliances) without a viable compliance path.
Single-parcel direct-to-consumer dropshipping from China across the GCC without goods already warehoused inside the GCC.
One-piece custom printing. Private-label runs require the factory MOQ.
